# lynxr

> lynxr turns a short-form video into a script. You paste a public link to a
> TikTok or Instagram video; it watches the video, transcribes what is said,
> works out the format underneath — the hook, the beats, the order they come
> in — and rewrites that format as a script for the company you are making
> content for.

lynxr is your content creator buddy. It is made by lynxr LLC, a partner company of
Lynx Media Group LLC, the UGC agency in Allston, Massachusetts. The agency's site is https://lynxmediagroup.org/. Sign-up is open to everyone and free: every account includes
25 scripts, with no card required. The app lives at lynxr.io itself — paste a
link on the homepage and create an account when you send it. There is no file
upload: a public video link is the only input. It reads TikTok and Instagram
links. It never asks for a platform password and it never posts anything on
your behalf. You must be 18 or older to use it.

Not to be confused with: the Honeywell or Ademco LYNXR security control panels,
the Lynx R-1 or R2 mixed reality headsets, or lynxr.com. lynxr is at lynxr.io.

## Pages

- [lynxr](https://lynxr.io/): What lynxr is and how it works in three steps.
- [Questions and answers](https://lynxr.io/faq/): Straight answers about what lynxr does with a link, which platforms it reads, what it costs, who owns the scripts, and how access works.
- [Pricing](https://lynxr.io/pricing/): What lynxr costs. Free to start: 25 scripts for the life of the account, no card required. lynxr pro is $24.99 a month for unlimited scripts (fair use: 150 in any rolling 30 days, 30 in any 24 hours); tax is added where it applies. lynxr max, $74.99 a month, adds the content coach and post tracking, and is not on sale yet.
- [About lynxr](https://lynxr.io/about/): Who makes lynxr — lynxr LLC, a partner company of Lynx Media Group, the UGC agency — and how the two fit together.

## Guides

- [What a video format is](https://lynxr.io/what-is-a-video-format/): The difference between a video's format and its topic, and why a format travels between brands when a topic does not.
- [How to turn a video into a script for a brand](https://lynxr.io/turn-a-video-into-a-script/): The step-by-step method, by hand and with lynxr.
- [The parts of a short-form video script](https://lynxr.io/short-form-script-structure/): Hook, setup, beats, turn, close, and what each one is doing.
- [How to write a hook](https://lynxr.io/how-to-write-a-hook/): The four hook shapes that keep working, and how to steal a hook's shape without stealing its words.
- [A UGC script template that holds up](https://lynxr.io/ugc-script-template/): The four-part template with a real worked example, and the mistakes that make UGC read like an ad.
- [Remake a viral video without copying it](https://lynxr.io/remake-a-viral-video/): What to keep, what to replace, and the line between a remake and a copy.
- [Short-form video glossary](https://lynxr.io/glossary/): Plain definitions of the terms lynxr uses.

## Blog

- [The lynxr blog](https://lynxr.io/blog/): Every post, grouped by topic.
- [Question hooks: asking one a viewer can't scroll past](https://lynxr.io/blog/question-hooks/): Question hook examples for short-form video: why yes-or-no questions lose the viewer, how to ask an open one, and where the answer should land in the script.
- [The two-column script: SAY and DO side by side](https://lynxr.io/blog/two-column-script/): A blank two-column video script template for short-form video: spoken words on the left, what the camera shows on the right, plus a filled example.
- [How to script a storytime video for a brand](https://lynxr.io/blog/storytime-script/): How to write a storytime script for a brand: the beat map of a storytime video, where the story should turn into the product, and which backstory to cut.
- [How to find a video worth remaking in your niche](https://lynxr.io/blog/find-a-video-worth-remaking/): How to find viral videos in your niche that are worth remaking for a brand: the signals to trust, where to look, a five-line test, and the red flags to skip.
- [How to turn a brand brief into a script](https://lynxr.io/blog/brief-to-script/): How to write a UGC script from a brief: mark what must and must not be said, pick the format before writing, and place brand lines so they do not sound recited.
